title: The indefinido and the imperfecto: events and background

sections.content: You know the *indefinido* and the *imperfecto* from A2 Unit 22. The *indefinido* tells the events that moved the story forward (*ordenó la invasión*, *se rindieron*). The *imperfecto* describes the situation around them (*el país vivía una crisis*, *muchos apoyaban la decisión*). The story of the Malvinas war needs both.

items.spanish: En 1981 la economía estaba en crisis, y cada vez más personas protestaban.
items.english: In 1981 the economy was in crisis, and more and more people were protesting.

items.spanish: El 2 de abril de 1982, el gobierno ordenó la invasión de las islas Malvinas.
items.english: On 2 April 1982, the government ordered the invasion of the Malvinas Islands.

items.spanish: Al principio, muchos argentinos apoyaban la decisión y celebraban en la plaza.
items.english: At first, many Argentines supported the decision and celebrated in the square.

items.spanish: El 14 de junio de 1982, las tropas argentinas se rindieron.
items.english: On 14 June 1982, the Argentine troops surrendered.

sections.content: A date or a sudden event usually calls for the *indefinido* (*el 14 de junio se rindieron*). "At that time", "at first" or "every day" usually calls for the *imperfecto* (*al principio apoyaban*).
